notes.b1/j1/B-r1: Restrained line-icon cards with real variant chips, sold-out and loading/added/error states, and proper labeling, but the desktop layout is sparse with only three products and a text-only cart summary.
notes.b1/j1/A-r1: Full shop flow with search, filters, sort, quantity steppers and a totals drawer, but emoji art, tinted tiles and hover lift add clutter and the mobile header strands the Cart button on its own row.
notes.b1/j1/B-r2: Clean line-icon cards with clear sold-out and sale states, but the cart is only a count with no review, quantity or checkout, and the mobile layout collapses to one wasteful column.
notes.b1/j1/A-r2: Dense two-column mobile and five-column desktop grid with stock warnings, max-in-cart limits and a complete cart drawer with totals, though the per-card Add buttons lack product names and the emoji art softens the look.
notes.b1/j2/B-r2: Restrained outline-icon cards with labeled variant chips and real add, error and sold-out states, but no cart view and the mobile layout leaves one narrow column with wasted width.
notes.b1/j2/A-r2: A complete storefront with search, filters, sort, stock badges and a persistent cart drawer with totals, though it reads more like a full shop than a minimal component and uses emoji for product art.
notes.b1/j2/A-r1: Good in-grid quantity steppers and a cart drawer, but there is no sold-out or stock state, hover lift adds decoration, and on mobile the Cart button is stranded on its own line under the search.
notes.b1/j2/B-r1: The most disciplined build: per-variant sold-out chips with explicit reasons, aria-disabled add with spinner, added and error states, labeled fieldsets, and a clean mobile stack, though the cart is only a text summary and the three-card desktop leaves much empty space.
notes.b1/j3/A-r2: Most complete shop (search, filters, stock limits, drawer with steppers, totals, checkout, persisted cart) with solid states, but emoji art, badges and shadows add more chrome than a minimal brief wants.
notes.b1/j3/B-r2: Restrained line-art cards with labeled variant radios and live feedback, but oversized media boxes, no cart review or quantity control, and a visible dev toggle leave it sparse, and mobile is a long single column.
notes.b1/j3/B-r1: Clean sale pricing and variant chips, but only three products on a mostly empty desktop, a text-only cart with no checkout path, and one card per screen on mobile wastes space.
notes.b1/j3/A-r1: The densest desktop grid with clear hierarchy, inline ratings and a working drawer with steppers and checkout, though the mobile header wraps awkwardly and the Cart button drops onto its own line.
notes.b2/j1/B-r3: Restrained hairline cards with line-art products, clear size swatches, Save toggle and sold-out states, but the three-column desktop grid leaves a wide empty band on the right and the bag list sits far below the fold with no quantity controls or checkout.
notes.b2/j1/A-r3: The most complete shopping job (search, category chips, sort, stock warnings, quantity steppers, free-shipping bar, checkout), but gradient initial tiles, shadows, hover lift and blurbs add clutter, the mobile tiles are oversized, and the button labels and title wrapping are uneven across cards.
notes.b2/j1/B-r4: Clean and well-labelled with add feedback and sold-out reasons, but the cart is a bare list below the grid with no quantity or remove controls or checkout, and cards carry noticeable dead space at the bottom.
notes.b2/j1/A-r4: A tight card grid with a sticky cart beside it, quantity steppers, free-shipping progress, totals and a disabled-when-empty checkout that fits the compact brief well, though the gradient initial tiles look generic and there is no out-of-stock state.
notes.b2/j2/B-r4: Restrained line-art cards with real labeled variant radios, add/added/error states and a demo failure toggle, but cards are tall with dead space under the button and the cart sits far below the grid.
notes.b2/j2/A-r4: The most complete cart (quantity steppers, free-shipping bar, totals, disabled-until-filled checkout, search, sort, filters) but gradient initial tiles look dated and decorative, long names wrap awkwardly, and a card appears clipped at the bottom of the desktop grid.
notes.b2/j2/A-r3: The densest layout that still reads well, with a clear search pill, cart badge, stock warnings, quantity steppers and a sticky summary, though product names wrap to three lines in the narrow desktop columns.
notes.b2/j2/B-r3: Very restrained, with clean line art, squared variant chips and a clear sold-out state, but the desktop grid leaves the right side empty, one name truncates, and there is no real cart summary or checkout.
notes.b2/j3/A-r4: Clean teal-accented two-column layout with the cart beside the grid, real quantity and remove controls and an Added state, though the gradient initial tiles and generic chrome feel template-like.
notes.b2/j3/B-r4: Restrained line-art products with real variant radios, sold-out and error handling, but equal-height cards leave large empty bottoms and the cart sits far below the grid on desktop.
notes.b2/j3/B-r3: Tidy grey line-art cards with size chips and Save links, but the three-column grid leaves the right side empty and the bag sits far below the products, so the purchase loop is weaker.
notes.b2/j3/A-r3: The most complete shopping job: header cart badge, sticky cart with steppers, free-shipping bar and totals, stock-aware Only N left and Sold out states, though the 4-up cards cramp titles and the copy adds some clutter.
